in_hebrew.name: נַעֲמָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נַעֲמָה הִיא שֵׁם עִבְרִי שֶׁפִּירוּשׁוֹ נָעִים, הָיְתָה בַּת לָמֶךְ וּצְחָר, וַתְּהִי אֵשֶׁת נֹחַ, וְהִיא הָיְתָה אֵם לִשְׁלֹשֶׁת בָּנִים, שֵׁם זֶה מְבַטָא אֶת הַיֹּפִי וְהַחֵן

in_greek.name: Νααμά
in_greek.long_meaning: η Νααμά είναι όνομα εβραϊκής προέλευσης που σημαίνει γλυκύτητα, χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη ως όνομα μιας από τις γυναίκες του Λάμεχ, και έχει μια σημαντική θέση στην εβραϊκή και χριστιανική παράδοση ως σύμβολο της ομορφιάς και της χάριτος

in_latin.name: Naama
in_latin.long_meaning: Naama est nomen Hebraicum quod significat suavitas, in Veteri Testamento ut nomen uxoris Lamech, et habet locum importantem in traditione Hebraica et Christiana ut symbolum pulchritudinis et gratiae

in_english.name: Naamah
in_english.long_meaning: Naamah is a Hebrew name meaning sweetness and pleasantness, used in the Old Testament as the name of Lamech's wife, and holds significant importance in Christian tradition as a symbol of beauty and elegance, often associated with qualities of kindness and charm

biblical_reference.note: Naamah is mentioned as the wife of Lamech and the daughter of Enoch

data.cultural_impact: The Hebrew name Naamah holds a rich cultural history, rooted in the belief of creating a pleasant and comforting environment. In ancient Jewish folklore, Naamah is one of the seven Hebrew daughters of the biblical patriarch Jacob, symbolizing peace, harmony, and a joyful family life. Aside from this, there is also a suggestion that Naamah might have been a Semitic goddess of fertility given her pleasant meaning.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Naamah can serve as a reminder of the comforting presence of God. In times of hardship and difficulties, it can evoke a sense of peace and serenity. It represents the unwavering love and continuous care of the divine force. Furthermore, the name Naamah can inspire one to be a source of comfort and joy for others, emulating the kindness and compassion rooted in its meaning.

historical_references.reference: According to Jewish mythology, Naamah was a sister of the biblical patriarchs Job and his three friends, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. She was considered a goddess of fertility and beauty.

In the apocryphal book of Jubilees, Naamah is mentioned as the wife of Lamech, the great-grandfather of Noah. She is described as a beautiful woman, whom Lamech married in order to appease God's anger after he had killed a man in a fit of rage.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Naamah in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Naamah, which means "Comfort or delight". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
